cards.text: Psalm 100 is a short one, friend: five verses, labeled a psalm of thanksgiving. It opens with a call to make a joyful noise to the LORD. A joyful NOISE, baker. Finally, a choir I qualify for!

cards.question: Who does the psalm call to make a joyful noise to the LORD?

cards.text: Next, the psalm says to serve the LORD. And I know, serving can sound like a shift where you stare at the clock the WHOLE time.

cards.question: The psalm doesn't want clock-watching. It says to serve the LORD with ___.
True or false: Psalm 100 tells people to come into the LORD's presence quietly.

cards.text: Then the psalm stops the party for something to know: "Know that the LORD is God."

cards.question: Right after saying the LORD is God, the psalm says who made us. Who is it?
True or false: Psalm 100 says the people the LORD made belong to Him.

cards.text: Then the psalm reaches for a picture from the fields: His pasture. I've never grazed a day in my life, friend, but even I know who hangs out in a pasture.

cards.question: Psalm 100 says we are His people, and the ___ of His pasture.

cards.text: Now the picture moves from the field to His gates and His courts. Friend, NOBODY walks through an open gate faster than a stamper who spent years waiting for a drawer to open.

cards.question: This is a psalm of thanksgiving, so it says to enter the LORD's gates with ___.
True or false: Along with entering His gates and courts, Psalm 100 says to give thanks to Him and bless His name.

cards.text: Then the last verse gives the reason. The reason for the noise, the reason for the gladness, the reason for ALL the thanks!

cards.question: Why does Psalm 100 call for all this thanks to the LORD?
How long does Psalm 100 say the LORD's loving devotion endures?
True or false: Psalm 100 says the LORD's faithfulness lasts for just one generation.

cards.text: I got swapped for a shiny new stamper after a few good years, friend. His faithfulness? It continues to ALL generations.

findings.problem: The opening card has 4 sentences: 'Psalm 100 is a short one...', 'It opens with a call...', 'A joyful NOISE, baker.', 'Finally, a choir I qualify for!'

rule.text: The opening card can be up to 3 sentences. It says who is speaking, to whom, and what is going on.

findings.problem: The question says 'This is a psalm of thanksgiving, so it says to enter the LORD's gates with ___.' The text never says verse 4 calls for thanksgiving because of the superscription. The 'so' adds a reason, and it links the label to the line in a way the text doesn't state.

rule.text: Reasons: He never adds why someone did, said or thought something unless the text says why.

findings.problem: The second half of verse 4, entering 'His courts with praise,' is never told or asked. Cards 11 and 13 mention His courts, but the baker never learns that the psalm calls for entering them with praise.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: The last story card repeats that His faithfulness continues to all generations. Card 17 just tested that fact. The card doesn't move the passage forward. It recaps a fact the baker already has.

'I got swapped for a shiny new stamper after a few good years' changes the backstory. He served the Millers for many years ('Years of good baking'), long enough to get worn down and for the cutters to arrive one at a time over the years. It was not 'a few good years.'

rule.text: His own world isn't Bible fact. His backstory, family, bakery and mission are the Dorinverse story in this file. He can talk about them freely, but never adds anything new to them.
